extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO, OED staff, and disciplinary authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state bar resignation/in-lieu-of-disbarment and describing procedural requirements, grounds for exclusion, and notice/publication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must mail a Notice and Order to the respondent at the last known address and provide an opportunity to file a response within forty days under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d). If mailed service is returned as undeliverable, service by publication in the Official Gazette is permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example facts: Notice and Order mailed March 7, 2012 to last known address; returned 'unclaimed' on March 28, 2012; served by publication in the Official Gazette on April 24 and May 1, 2012; respondent had more than forty days since second publication but did not request copies or file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond supports finding of no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response following proper notice/publication, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, respondent's failure to request documents or respond after Official Gazette publication led to the determination that no genuine issue existed and exclusion was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed disbarred definition (basis for reciprocal discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, a practitioner is deemed to be disbarred if he or she is disbarred, excluded on consent, or has resigned in lieu of a disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state bar resignation in lieu of disbarment (Notice of Resignation in Lieu of Disbarment) is therefore sufficient to trigger reciprocal discipline proceedings before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion may be ordered for violations of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the respondent's state-bar disbarment/resignation based on conduct involving misrepresentations and a felony conviction as supporting this violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct: criminal acts and dishonesty (RPC 8.4(b) and 8.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal acts that reflect adversely on a lawyer's honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness (RPC 8.4(b)) and conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation (RPC 8.4(c)) constitute professional misconduct and support disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statement of Alleged Misconduct states respondent committed False Statements (18 U.S.C. § 1001), and concluded that by committing that crime he violated RPC 8.4(b) and/or RPC 8.4(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentations to third parties as basis for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Material misrepresentations made to third parties (here, a bank and the United States Small Business Association) during representation can be the factual basis for state disciplinary charges and consequent reciprocal discipline by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statement of Alleged Misconduct details actions with respect to material misrepresentations made to a bank and the SBA during representation of the owner/seller of a company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal conviction (18 U.S.C. § 1001) as disciplinary support
rubrics_metrics.description: A guilty plea or conviction for making false statements in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1001 (a felony) is cited as conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice and supports disciplinary measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references the filing of a Felony Information and a guilty plea to False Statements on October 20, 2010, as part of the basis for state disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion (non-patent practice before the USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion ordered applies to the practice of trademark and other non‑patent law before the USPTO; respondents not registered as patent practitioners are not authorized to practice patent law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifically: 'Respondent is excluded from the practice of trademark and other non‑patent law before the USPTO effective the date of this Final Order' and notes respondent is not a registered patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and interagency notice obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and give notice of public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where respondent is admitted, and the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs publication of a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette (text provided) and notification to appropriate agencies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority, specifically 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutes and regulations as the legal basis for the exclusion and publication/notification directives.
